description: Fleet overview and per-host details for Windows hosts monitored by windows_exporter.

panels.description: One row per scraped host. Click a hostname to open its details below. Services up counts running services; Auto stopped counts services with start mode auto that are not running.

targets.expr: (max by (instance, product, version) (windows_os_info{job=~"$job"})) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}
(100 * (1 - avg by (instance) (rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"$job", mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])))) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}

(max by (instance) (100 * (1 - windows_logical_disk_free_bytes{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"} / windows_logical_disk_size_bytes{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"}))) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}
(sum by (instance) (windows_service_state{job=~"$job", state="running"})) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}

(count by (instance) (windows_service_state{job=~"$job", state="running"} == 0 and on (instance, name) windows_service_start_mode{job=~"$job", start_mode="auto"} == 1)) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}

panels.title: Hosts

panels.description: Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.

targets.expr: topk(25, (100 * (1 - avg by (instance) (rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"$job", mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

panels.title: CPU utilization

panels.description: Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.

targets.expr: topk(25, (max by (instance) (100 * (1 - windows_memory_physical_free_bytes{job=~"$job"} / windows_memory_physical_total_bytes{job=~"$job"}))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

panels.title: Memory utilization

panels.description: Sum over all interfaces. Received is drawn below the axis. Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.

targets.expr: topk(25, (sum by (instance) (rate(windows_net_bytes_sent_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8)) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

topk(25, (sum by (instance) (rate(windows_net_bytes_received_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8)) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

panels.title: Network throughput

panels.description: Sum over all volumes. Read is drawn below the axis. Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.

targets.expr: topk(25, (sum by (instance) (rate(windows_logical_disk_write_bytes_total{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

topk(25, (sum by (instance) (rate(windows_logical_disk_read_bytes_total{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

panels.title: Disk throughput

panels.description: Time since the last boot.
panels.title: Uptime

panels.description: Committed virtual memory as a share of the commit limit (physical memory + page files). Allocations fail at 100%.
panels.title: Commit used

panels.description: Services with start mode "auto" that are not running. See the Services row for names.

targets.expr: count(windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state="running"} == 0 and on (name) windows_service_start_mode{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", start_mode="auto"} == 1) or vector(0)

panels.title: Stopped auto services

panels.description: Share of total CPU time across all logical processors.

targets.expr: sum by (mode) (rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", mode!="idle"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(count(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", mode="idle"}))

panels.title: CPU utilization by mode

panels.description: Processor queue length counts threads ready to run but waiting for a CPU. A sustained value above 2 per core indicates CPU contention. Context switches and interrupts use the right axis.
panels.title: Processor queue, context switches and interrupts

panels.description: Available memory is the standby (cache), free and zero page lists.
panels.title: Physical memory

panels.description: Committed virtual memory against the commit limit (physical memory + page files).
panels.title: Commit charge

panels.description: Hard page faults read from or written to disk. Sustained page reads indicate memory pressure.
panels.title: Paging

panels.description: Share of time the volume was servicing requests (1 - idle time).
panels.title: Volume busy time

panels.description: Reads are drawn below the axis.
panels.title: Disk throughput

panels.description: Reads are drawn below the axis.
panels.title: Disk IOPS

panels.description: Average time per read and write operation.
panels.title: Disk latency

panels.description: Average number of read and write requests queued for the volume. A queue that stays high while latency rises indicates a disk bottleneck. The avg_*_requests_queued metrics grow like counters, so the panel takes their rate.
panels.title: Disk queue length

panels.description: Received traffic is drawn below the axis.
panels.title: Network throughput

panels.description: Sent plus received traffic relative to the link speed reported by the adapter. Interfaces without a link speed are not shown.
panels.title: Network utilization

panels.description: Services configured to start automatically that are not in the running state. Delayed-start and trigger-start services may show up here until they start.

targets.expr: max by (name, state) (windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"} == 1) and on (name) (windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state="running"} == 0) and on (name) (windows_service_start_mode{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", start_mode="auto"} == 1)

panels.title: Automatic services not running

panels.description: Number of time sources the NTP client uses. 0 means the clock is not synchronized.
panels.title: NTP time sources

panels.description: Absolute offset between the system clock and the selected time source.
panels.title: Clock offset

panels.title: Collector duration
